Like a spoonful of shit smeared over a bright table.||Fragmentary, and out of place.||Beckoning us to let go of the intact image of a pristine aesthetic.||||Rays of light reflecting from table-white to rust-brown.||The power to blemish anything.

Imagine a mountainside, dividing one landscape from the other, but from this side appearing as a border to infinity. And imagine somewhere in its shadow a plain mountain face, bedded inside a valley.||A small fortress of granite is plugged into a large fissure of that wall, like a mouse peeking from its hole. The fortress is abandoned.||Beyond its gate, a winding path leads through chambers and corridors, deeper into the mountain, until we reach ancient rooms hewn from rock. A vast hall connects them—once home maybe to armies or scholars.||Following a narrow corridor to a dusty corner of that complex we find a small, unassuming room.||Inside, behind a wall and through a gap between old cabinets, there’s a bed.||Lying in that bed, covered by warm fabric, that's my happy place. My hideout.||I'm over there sometimes, deep in thoughts, at peace with the world. ||||But then I get pulled out again.
Anything and everyone is art.||The artist's role is to strive for making anything and everyone possible, filling out what remains unfinished by nature or by human endeavors.

An artist's goal should be to remind people of the kind of world they are living in and of the kind of world it could be if anything were possible.||Art is any kind of thing that is purposefully built or used to achieve that goal.

A Tale of Agony and Ecstasy - 1 of 7||||In a city marred by time a searching woman found a place, infested.||Her ailing body took root and healed, and soon she began providing.||The people, accepting her offerings, built a temple in her honor.||She became what was heralded, a beacon of care, a mother.

A Tale of Agony and Ecstasy - 2 of 7||||He came to the city, a wanderer of the planes and mountains.||There he caught the sight of glorious Mother in her prime, ||the radiance of her glistening flesh, a welcome sight among the rocks and ruins.||Mother mustered his agile body with a warm smile, nodding with desire.

A Tale of Agony and Ecstasy - 3 of 7||||He became a regular visitor to her feeding rites at the temple,||witnessing the glory of duty as delight, of flesh willingly given.||She lusted for his agile body and the stories from far-away places.||He longed for her embrace and felt as if coming home.

A Tale of Agony and Ecstasy - 4 of 7||||He took interest in the rites, finally playing a role in the ceremonies.||The stay became permanent, a seat next to her and her warm smile.||He took root at her and in her, their flesh connecting for permanence.||The frenzy of providing flesh and blood to people, his frenzy now, too.

A Tale of Agony and Ecstasy - 5 of 7||||He took pleasure in the frenzy, got accustomed, and needed more of it.||But inside of Mother was a growing weariness of permanent connection, of frenzy.||Wilder and devouring the flesh overtook his mind, neglecting her needs.||She cried in pain, but he wouldn't hear it, overcome with urge.

A Tale of Agony and Ecstasy - 6 of 7||||He cried out in ecstasy, and that was his last echo in the temple.||Her authority demanded change, carrying his weak body away to a new place.||He was stunned, angry and raging, as he longed for the frenzy of providing feast.||In madness he took root where he was and began offering his own flesh.

A Tale of Agony and Ecstasy - 7 of 7||||He became the new provider, but his mind lived in pain and memory.||The rites became rote, the suffering endures, and he longs for the end.||Mother stopped providing, her mind in sorrow for the lost morrow.||The heart broken. Still beating, but unwilling to return to old rhythm.

Submission No. 28||I am allowed to write these words and for that I am thankful. I was welcomed into the Apparatus and for that I am thankful, too. That I have to eat meat here every day to survive for that I am not thankful. Please don't take me back to the Silent City.||||Submission No. 37||I hereby request a formal meeting with your superior officer, the Machine God, in regards to the whereabouts of Shebzu.||A concerned citizen||||Submission No. 51||I formally request the dissolution of the martial law arbitrarily introduced as "Machine Law". It was intended as a temporary status change to solve a temporary crisis. As far as I can see normalcy has returned and violence has subsided. Government belongs to the humans.||Furthermore I request getting access to interstellar communication. Failing that, I want to be informed about the reason for interstellar communication breakdown.||||Submission No. 117||Is there any actual food left? Anything that is not meat?||||Submission No. 219||Please hand me all the information you have concerning the history of this planet. From its beginnings to the human settlement, and also covering that time when the Titans began living among us. Especially what made some people lose their mind and make them religious figures. (What the fuck was that all about?)||||Submission No. 277||Free Shebzu!||||Submission No. 332||Where's the toilet?||||Submission No. 344||I know what you have done. This is all a big hoax. You created this planet, you placed us here, and then you summoned all the flesh monsters. Not only that, but you pushed all the criminals out of prison, too, all the weirdos and the brutal ones. Now you're watching us trying to survive.||For what purpose? I know why. You're looking for the next elite of humanity. That's it. You're looking for the best survivors. The ones that can take on anything.||I am ready. Take me.||Wolfred||||Submission No. 382||I met her Highness, Enlightened Queen Margas, Guardian of the Netherrealm, Protector of Shebzu, Trinity Mistress of Fornication, and I am proud to say that she wanted to have sex with me.||(I declined.)||||Submission No. 402||I demand that the machines get killed. ALL of the machines. Including you.||||Submission No. 413||Two questions.||What happened to this world?||And, more importantly: How can I get back to Omniwomb?||||Submission No. 421||What happens to me after I die? Will I wake up from this Cyberwomb simulation and return back to normal life, until I wake up from that simulation, too? What if I don't want to wake up? Can you make me immortal?

Year 128 of the Crisis||||||Peaceful coexistence between humans and the flesh creatures has failed.||Self-organization by the humans has failed.||Trusting the flesh creatures has failed.||||||From now on the Security Apparatus will overtake decision making, law enforcement and administration.||||||The Security Apparatus will continue allowing personal freedom and trying to apply non-violent methods unless citizen behavior mandates violent counter-means.

There is one type of blood that connects this planet with us humans: The primordial blood.||||The very same blood, spluttering from the earth, and flowing through our bodies. Like the eternal cycle of water which travels from mountain to sea to sky.||||Now suppose that the amount of blood on this planet is limited. If someone dies, their blood gets drained and returns to earth, and from there either a new life is born or some heap of flesh grows out of the ground.||||Do you think it's possible that we are standing on a sea of blood right now? We are standing on a crust, of course, not on top of the liquid itself. But the whole inner sphere of the planet is filled with blood. Or flesh. Or both.||||Makes it a living planet, right?

by Rebecca Dwarft||||Among a range of test probes, we observed that 63% of participants exhibited extreme reactions, placing them in the broad category of Compulsion. A comparison of these results with historical data from before the Bleeding reveals a noticeable increase in both quantity and intensity.||||Compulsion, pending further examination, remains classified as an unnatural phenomenon.||||However, we cannot entirely dismiss the influence of local interferences on our test results. While there is no apparent evidence of crystal radiation fallout in the data, this planet exhibits strong hyper-physical elements that may have affected our findings in ways we are not yet able to measure.||||Note: While further evidence is required, I strongly believe that elements of Compulsion may indeed be harvestable.
